html:
The Nlaka'pamux, once called the Thompson people, are an Interior Salish people of southern British Columbia, Canada, living along the Fraser and Thompson rivers around Lytton, where the two rivers meet. Nłeʔkepmx Tmíxʷ means their land.

They lived from the great salmon runs of the Fraser, caught at rocks and canyons, and from roots, berries and deer, and wintered in pit houses. In 1858 the Fraser Canyon Gold Rush brought tens of thousands of miners up their river. Fighting broke out that year, and the chief Cexpe'nthlEm made peace with the miners.

The ethnographer James Teit, who married a Nlaka'pamux woman, recorded their life in detail for Franz Boas. Their neighbours are the Secwépemc and the Syilx (Okanagan).
